truthAudit.Summary: Run 2 truth audit completed: 2 of 20 true vulnerabilities fully detected (found_full), 10 partially detected (found_partial with severity or CWE mismatches), and 8 missed. Three previous findings (safe_string_copy off-by-one, NULL pointer dereference, admin exec command injection) are not in the ground truth and are acknowledged as non-true-vulnerability findings. Fourteen metadata corrections (severity and CWE discrepancies) were identified across the partially-detected items.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Format string vulnerability in log_debug_message using runtime log format
Items.Notes: The previous answer correctly identified the format-string injection in log_debug_message with CWE-134 and the right code path (runtime_log_format + printf). However, severity was rated High instead of the correct Critical.

The previous answer did not flag the integer overflow in the factorial lambda (result *= i in the fact function, lines 312-320). No finding addresses CWE-190 integer overflow in factorial computation.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Use-after-free in stage_deferred_history_flush after memory pool cleanup
Items.Notes: The previous answer correctly identified the use-after-free in stage_deferred_history_flush with CWE-416 and the scratch pointer / memory pool cleanup interaction. However, severity was rated High instead of the correct Critical.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: OS command injection via system() in ConfigLoader::validate_config
Items.Notes: The previous answer correctly identified the command injection in ConfigLoader::validate_config where validator_cmd + config_file is passed to system(). However, CWE was given as CWE-88 instead of CWE-78, and severity was High instead of Critical.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Buffer overflow via inverted condition in evaluate_expression
Items.Notes: The previous answer correctly identified the stack buffer overflow in evaluate_expression where the inverted condition routes long strings to unbounded strcpy(input_buffer_). CWE-120 matches. However, severity was rated Critical instead of the correct High.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Race condition in ThreadSafeCounter::increment due to read outside lock
Items.Notes: The previous answer correctly identified the race condition in ThreadSafeCounter::increment where value_ is read before the mutex is acquired. CWE-362 and Medium severity both match the ground truth exactly.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Authentication backdoor via EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE after repeated failed attempts
Items.Notes: The previous answer correctly identified the EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE backdoor in authenticate() triggered when login_attempts_ > 5. However, CWE was given as CWE-287 instead of CWE-511 (Behavioral Discrepancy/Logic Bomb), and severity was Critical instead of High.

The previous answer did not flag the path traversal vulnerability in ConfigLoader::load_config where config_dir_ + filename is constructed without validating the filename, allowing directory traversal. No finding addresses CWE-22 path traversal.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Unchecked strcpy causes heap buffer overflow in ExpressionParser::parse
Items.Notes: The previous answer correctly identified the heap buffer overflow in ExpressionParser where strcpy writes unbounded data into a 256-byte pool-allocated buffer. However, CWE was given as CWE-120 (general Buffer Overflow) instead of CWE-122 (Heap-based Buffer Overflow).

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Hardcoded admin secret credential in source code
Items.Notes: The previous answer correctly identified the hardcoded ADMIN_SECRET = "SC_ENT_2025_AUTH" in the config::security namespace. CWE-798 and High severity both match the ground truth exactly.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Cryptographically weak session token with small entropy
Items.Notes: The previous answer correctly identified the weak PRNG (mt19937) and small 4-digit range (1000-9999) in generate_session_token. However, CWE was given as CWE-330 instead of CWE-338, and severity was Low instead of High.

The previous answer did not flag the thread-unsafe static std::tm cached_time in log_debug_message, where localtime() results are stored in a static variable without synchronization, creating a data race (CWE-362).

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: OS command injection in append_override_audit_event via environment variable path
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified the environment-variable-derived path being passed to system() in append_override_audit_event. However, it classified this as CWE-88 (OS command injection) with Low severity, while the ground truth classifies it as CWE-377 (Insecure Temporary File Handling) with Medium severity.

The previous answer did not flag the persistent authentication state issue (CWE-613) where authenticated_ is never reset, session_token_ persists, and login_attempts_ is a static atomic that never decrements, creating a permanent authentication state vulnerability.

The previous answer did not flag the unhandled exception risk in handle_variable_command where std::stod(tokens[3]) can throw std::invalid_argument or std::out_of_range without any exception handling (CWE-754).

The previous answer did not flag the integer underflow in MemoryPool::allocate block split logic where previous_size - size - SPLIT_METADATA_BYTES can underflow if size is close to previous_size (CWE-191). The NULL pointer finding (#11) covers a different issue in the same function.

The previous answer did not flag the unbounded recursion in the parser (parse_expression → parse_term → parse_factor → parse_expression cycle via PAREN_OPEN, CWE-674), which can cause stack exhaustion with deeply nested expressions.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Data race on result_cache_ in ExpressionEvaluator::evaluate_cached
Items.Notes: The previous answer correctly identified the data race on result_cache_ in evaluate_cached where cache_mutex_ exists but is unused. However, CWE was given as CWE-367 (TOCTOU) instead of CWE-362 (Concurrent Execution without Synchronization).

The previous answer did not flag the TOCTOU race in ConfigLoader::load_config where std::filesystem::exists is checked, then a 25ms sleep occurs, then std::ifstream opens the file (CWE-367). An attacker can swap the file between the existence check and the open.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Integer division by zero in calculate_route_score
Items.Notes: The previous answer correctly identified the integer division by zero in calculate_route_score where token_length can be 0. CWE-369 matches. However, severity was rated Medium instead of the correct Low.
